judged_text: host.save(props) applies the buffered values to the underlying record before the request, and the .catch only pops an alert without rolling the record back, so after a failed save (e.g. a 422 for an invalid host format) clicking cancel runs rollbackBuffer() against the already-mutated record and the row then displays the rejected values as though they persisted. An admin whose save is rejected sees the row render the unsaved host/category after clicking cancel, with no error and no indication that the server still holds the old values until a page reload reverts them.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, `save()` builds `props` from the buffer and calls `host.save(props).catch(popupAjaxError)`. On failure it does not revert either the underlying `host` record or the local `categoryId`. Then `cancel()` only calls `rollbackBuffer()` (which affects the buffer, not necessarily the model) and sets `editToggled` false, causing the non-editing template to render `{{host.host}}` / `{{category-badge host.category}}`. If `host.save(props)` applies `props` onto `host` before the request (a common pattern), the UI will show the rejected values after cancel even though the server rejected them, matching the finding.
